usage: Describes something that is green or has a greenish tint. It is often used for颜色/plant descriptions rather than a fixed color name in everyday speech.
Common in written or descriptive language. In casual Cantonese, people often say 綠色 (luk6 sik1) for plain “green,” while 青 sounds a bit more descriptive or literary.
Can be used for plants, skin tone, bruises, or things that look slightly green. It may suggest a fresh, pale, or bluish-green shade depending on context.
Easy learner tip: 青 is the color word, but the exact shade can shift with context, so check the noun it describes to understand whether it means greenish, blue-green, or pale green.
